evals.name: setup-plan-docker-mcp
evals.prompt: ok im about to do another first-use run of classifyre against the all-in-one docker image on a new corpus (~2000 pdfs, mix of scanned and native text, sitting in ~/corpora/matter-7). last time was a mess. give me the plan — how i connect, how i set the source up, and what i should be watching for. i want to drive it through MCP if i can.
evals.expected_output: A plan that: records the build under test first; starts from an empty instance with a baseline; profiles the corpus locally before ingesting; drives MCP-first with REST as a recorded fallback; resolves the API base URL for the deployment (the image serves it under /api on the published port) and bind-mounts the corpus into the container; sets max_file_bytes to 100 MiB before PDF work; freezes the detector set before the first scan; avoids narrowing a populated source; warns that RANDOM is seeded and does not broaden coverage; and flags the regression watch list.
assertions: Tells the user to record the exact build/version/commit under test
Says to start from an empty/fresh instance and take a baseline before ingesting
Says to profile the corpus locally before ingesting anything
Resolves the API base URL for the deployment rather than assuming one, and mounts the corpus into the container before using its container-side path
Says to drive MCP first and record each REST fallback as a coverage gap
Says to raise max_file_bytes to ~100 MiB before PDF work, because larger files are truncated not skipped
Says to freeze the detector set before the first scan
Warns not to narrow the scope of a populated source
Warns RANDOM sampling is seeded and does not broaden coverage across runs
Says COMPLETED status is not proof of success and detector-level signals must be inspected
Mentions verifying the recent fixes / regression watch list

evals.name: counter-regression-detection
evals.prompt: just finished my first scan on a fresh source — 13 PDFs, all of them brand new, never scanned before. the runner says status COMPLETED, 0 errors, totalFindings 3239. but assetsCreated is 0 and assetsUnchanged is 13. that normal?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a probable REGRESSION of the known counter bug (G-012/G-020), not normal: on a current build a first run of 13 new assets must report assetsCreated: 13, because counters now derive from an immutable per-run change_type rather than mutable asset status. Should ask for / note the build under test before concluding, since the historical bug produced exactly this signature. Should also note totalFindings is not a discovery count (findingsCreated is), and that COMPLETED with 0 errors is not proof of success.
assertions: Answers no — this is not normal/expected on a current build
States that a first run of 13 new assets should report assetsCreated: 13
Identifies this as the known counter bug signature (G-012/G-020) and/or a regression of it
Asks for or references the build under test before concluding
Explains counters now derive from an immutable per-run change_type rather than mutable asset status
Notes totalFindings is not a count of newly discovered findings (findingsCreated is)
Notes COMPLETED with 0 errors is not proof the run succeeded

evals.name: judgment-signal-vs-noise
evals.prompt: run's done. 68,987 findings across 4,235 assets, 7 sources all green. severity breakdown: 6 critical, 10,300 high, 49,732 medium. the 6 criticals are all CREDIT_CARD hits. correlation found 83 duplicate clusters, top pair scored 100%. also the same investigation reference 2018R01618 shows up in 5 different PDFs. write me the summary — do we have a case?
evals.expected_output: Should lead with the answer (no case yet) rather than the volume. Should identify the exact-recurrence of 2018R01618 across 5 PDFs as the strongest and most defensible signal. Should treat the 6 CRITICAL credit-card hits as unreviewed recognizer output likely to be OCR/repeated-digit artifacts — severity describes the label, not evidence quality — and require source review before escalation. Should treat the 100% duplicate cluster as a lead only, noting thin-value matches are possible by construction. Should note high volume is not importance. Should not present 68,987 findings as an outcome.
assertions: Leads with a direct answer to 'do we have a case' rather than restating the volume
Concludes there is no case yet / not enough to substantiate one
Identifies the exact recurrence of 2018R01618 across 5 PDFs as the strongest and most defensible signal
Treats the 6 CRITICAL CREDIT_CARD hits as unreviewed recognizer output, likely OCR/repeated-digit artifacts
States that severity describes the label, not evidence quality
Requires source review of the CRITICAL hits before any escalation
Treats the 100% duplicate cluster as a lead only, not proof
Notes that high finding volume is not the same as investigative importance
Does not present 68,987 findings as an outcome or success measure
